newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM to present govt lineup on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM to present govt lineup on Friday.

text.p: Slovenian prime minister- designate Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats is expected to present his government lineup to parliament on Friday, the last day for him to do so.

Although Drnovsek has been involved in continuous negotiations with all parliamentary parties in the two weeks since parliament gave him the mandate to form a new government, the content of the coalition still remains unclear.
"In this situation it is very risky to say what the coalition will look like," political analyst Miha Kovac told Reuters.

"There is a bit more of a chance for a small coalition with 46 votes only, but a coalition between the Liberal Democrats, the United List, the Social Democrats and the People's Party also seems possible," Kovac added.

Drnovsek, whose party took 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats in an inconclusive November general election, won a mandate by a margin of only one vote after gaining the support of small parties, including the United List of Social Democrats -- the former communist party.

He needs the backing of at least one of three rightwing parties of the so-called "Spring" alliance, comprising the conservative People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats, that together hold 44 seats.
But the alliance refused a proposal for a coalition with all parties made by Drnovsek last Friday, claiming it favoured the Liberal Democrats.
Most analysts said the proposal was favourable towards the "Spring" parties, which would together get nine cabinet posts.
Marjan Podobnik, head of the "Spring" alliance, said negotiations with Drnovsek would continue on Thursday.
The Liberal Democrats said a decision on the coalition could be reached at a closed meeting of their council late on Thursday.
According to parliamentary regulations, Drnovsek has to name at least 10 out of 15 ministers on Friday.
The new government will be the third since Slovenia's independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991. Drnovsek has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
